steps.text: Preheat an oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease 12 muffin cups, or line with paper muffin liners.

Combine the oat bran and wheat bran in a large bowl. Stir in sour cream and milk. Allow mixture to stand for 10 minutes. Combine flour, baking powder, baking soda, brown sugar, and salt in a separate bowl. Gently stir blueberries into the flour mixture, carefully coating all the blueberries with flour. Stir vegetable oil, orange juice and zest, egg, and vanilla extract into the bran mixture. Combine flour mixture with the wet ingredients until just blended. Drop batter into lined muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 15 to 20 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before removing to cool completely on a wire rack.

raw_recipe.headline: Blueberry Orange Bran Muffin

review.reviewBody: Really good tasting muffin! I used WW flour instead of AP flour. The blueberries really made these muffins moist and for my taste I think it had too many blueberries as it went mushy. So, next time I will decrease the berries. The orange flavour was really nice and delicate, it didn't overpower the bran muffin. We really liked this muffin. Thx.

These are the best bran muffins, and I've tried a lot of recipes. I do make a few alterations, but they are very tasty either with or without the alterations. I use 1 1/2 cups wheat bran and omit the oat bran (it's just easier to find in the store). I also sub whole wheat flour for the all purpose flour. Last, I add 2 TBSP of flax meal to the wheat bran. If you can find boreal blueberries (I buy them frozen at Trader Joes), they are perfect for this recipe. They are a smaller blueberry and work well in muffins.

You NEED to let these sit at least 8 hours before taking a bite, trust me on this. Although they smell wonderful right out of the oven, they won't taste good until they have had time to sit and let the flavors meld. 

These muffins freeze very well. Just pull one out of the freezer at night and let thaw in the fridge or counter and they are perfect for breakfast the next day.

I used 1 c. bran and 1 1/2 c. flour, and melted butter instead of oil (I try to avoid refined oils). I also had to add more milk, but I live at a high altitude and often adjust by increasing the liquid. They turned out moist, delicious, and not mushy.

These were truly delicious! Not mushy at all as others have suggested. I had to make some changes only because of what I had available, but I think I would make the exact same changes next time! 1. Used vanilla Greek yogurt instead of sour cream. 2. Used lemon juice/zest instead or orange (only about half a lemon juice because I was afraid of the mush factor) 3. Did not have oat bran so I ground up quick oats in the food processor and it worked great! 4. Added some chia seeds. 5. Also added a strussel topping (2tbs butter, 1/3 c brown sugar, 1/4c flour, 1 tbs cinnamon). Seriously so good. My 6 and 3 year olds loved them too!

I used just wheat bran as that is what I had. I also cut the brown sugar to less then 1/2 a cup as I do not like a sweet muffin, that is a cup cake. I did add a few more blueberries to us up what size had I baked 18 minutes at 400f. They were great !

This is a very tasty muffin. I made it as stated and it was great. The second time I made it I followed some of the other suggestions and I used Whole Wheat flour instead of all purpose flour, 3/4 cup blueberries and only half of a navel orange for the juice and zest. With these changes it made them fantastic. I think I might try clementines next time. I now make this once a week instead of my banana muffins.

Great recipe! But, I made quite a few changes:
2/3 cup blueberries (frozen) 
splenda instead of sugar
2 Tbsp oil
2 Tbsp applesauce
yogurt instead of sour cream
1 whole orange (blended)
1 1/2 cups wheat bran, no oat bran

Delicious and healthy :) They are quite moist, so make sure you don't under cook them.

I love these! I did have to sub a bit. My husband is diabetic so I used WW Pastry Flour instead of AP. I thought I had blueberries, but only had blackberries. Luckily, they were really sweet. I cut them in half. My middle son also ate my last orange, so I had to sub a sweet grapefruit. I only used 1/3 cup of brown sugar & added 1/3 a cup of Splenda. They are nutty, moist & flavorful. This will be my go to healthy muffin from now on. Endless possibilities. Thanks for sharing!
Great! Baked in mini muffin tins. Made 48, baked for 10 minutes.

I make these regularly, using the wheat bran leftover from sifting my freshly ground wheat. I use freshly ground white whole wheat flour (not sifted), and yogurt in place of the sour cream. Occasionally I need a little extra yogurt, since the WW flour is more dense, but they always turn out great! A full cup of blueberries is a bit too much for us -- 2/3 cup is plenty.

Fabulous healthy muffin! Moist, great texture and perfectly sweetend. I made a few adjustments ... used All-Bran cereal for the wheat bran (just let it soak longer)... and only had two measly tangerines for juice, so I added a heaping tablespoon on orange marmalade. Used apple butter for half of the oil to cut down on the fat. Great! Will definately make again. Even my kids loved it!

This recipe is so much better tasting than muffins I have bought at bakeries And it is healthier! I substituted frozen cranberries for the blueberries and add toasted walnuts for protein. I have one with my coffee every morning . Delicious ! I also use avocado oil. Everyone who comes to my house wants to know if I have any muffins! I am going to start to hide them or lie or they are all gone.

Good recipe. I didn’t have oat bran, so I substituted the oat bran with whole wheat flour. I used 4 tablespoons of orange juice for the juice and zest. It was good, but I plan to make it the next time with the oat bran and the wheat bran, as the recipe instructs. I did have fresh blueberries. I thought that the muffins were a bit dry, so I will add 5 tablespoons of orange juice instead of four.
I liked this recipe used both oat and wheat bran. The only substitution I made was I used frozen blueberries and it turned out pretty good. I’ll be making these again.
I followed the recipe exactly as written, and the muffins tuned out delicious! This recipe is definitely a keeper
I didn't have Oat Bran so used all Wheat Bran. Not too bad but a bit too much bran.
Substituted chopped dates for the blueberries - delicious! I like the subtle orange flavouring. Found they were moist but not too mushy, although they needed the full 20min baking time.
Delicious! great recipe if you are looking for healthy blueberry muffins.
Reduced blueberries to 1/2 cup and used gluten-free flour. My four neighbors (&I) loved them. Next time, I will add chopped nuts & dried cranberries.
